title: An early-stage clinical trial to establish whether a new type of antibacterial (known as SASPject PT3.9) is a safe and effective way of treating people living with cystic fibrosis who have lung infections caused by the bacterium, Pseudomonas aeruginosa
official: A first-in-human, phase 1b/2a randomised controlled trial to establish safety, tolerability and early efficacy of the phage-based antimicrobial SASPject PT3.9, for treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in people living with cystic fibrosis
summary:
Background and study aims
STEPS-CF is a first-in-human, placebo controlled, randomised, double blinded (i.e. patient and clinicians are both unaware whether individual participants are given the drug or a placebo) clinical trial. The trial will be carried out in England, and will test safety, tolerability and initial efficacy (clinical effects) of SASPject PT3.9, a phage therapy treatment of lung infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P.a), in adults living with Cystic Fibrosis. SASPject PT3.9 will be given by intravenous infusion (via a vein). SASPject PT3.9 is a novel antibacterial developed by the UK study sponsor, SASPiPhi Limited, and is based on a modified bacteriophage, a virus which only infects and kills bacteria.   

Who can participate?
Study participants will be adults living with Cystic Fibrosis with lung infection due to a SASPject PT3.9-sensitive P.a, confirmed by testing of sputum samples before study enrolment. Study duration is up to 63 days for each participant. 

What does the study involve?
This STEPS-CF trial has been designed in three parts. Part A is a (Phase 1b) single ascending dose (SAD) study: 12 participants, in 4 dose level cohorts, will each receive a single dose of SASPject PT3.9. The dose levels will be tested in order, from low to high. Once a dose level is shown to be tolerated, the next dose level cohort will be tested. The maximum tolerated SAD dose will then be used in Part B of the study, a (Phase 1b) multiple ascending dose (MAD) study. 8 participants will receive SASPject PT3.9 or placebo doses up to twice daily, for three days. Successful completion of Part B of the study will allow entry into Part C (Phase 2a), an extension of the MAD study with 24
participants, using the tolerated MAD dosing.   

STEPS-CF will assess SASPject PT3.9 safety, tolerability and its effect on the human body including lung function tests and blood tests, the antibiotic effect on P.a bacteria in sputum samples, and participant experience of SASPject PT3.9 treatment, including quality of life questionnaires.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Benefits:
SASPject PT3.9 is a therapeutic intended to combat lung infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P.a). It will be administered to people living with cystic fibrosis who have tested positive for P.a lung infection, and may provide the patient benefits associated with the alleviation of an infection. In addition, participants will receive attention from qualified medical professionals, in the form of monitoring in the clinical research unit during administration of the treatment and in follow up visits for the following 60 days.
Risks:
* There is a potential for infusion site reactions. To mitigate this, participants will be monitored for at least 8 hours post dose. Appropriate medications to treat any infusion site reactions will be available in case of need. Depending on severity of the reaction, the investigator will immediately take appropriate countermeasures. If there are infusion reactions, the infusion will be stopped immediately and appropriate treatment provided.
* Other unexpected adverse effects are possible due to the novel nature of this therapy. To minimise the risk of this, the trial is designed to start with sentinel patients at low doses and gradually increase the dose in successive steps, introducing more trial participants at higher doses only if lower doses are determined to be safe. Signs of serious adverse events will cause the study to be ended prematurely.
* A degree of pain and discomfort may be caused by the administration of the treatment and follow up sampling, although this is expected to be low. Unexpected adverse events may also lead to participants experiencing pain and discomfort. Expert medical attention will be available to mitigate the medical consequences of such an event.
* Abstaining from alcohol 48h in advance of screening visit may be an inconvenience for some participants.
* The requirement for residence at CRU and to attend follow up appointments will create a degree of inconvenience for study participants. However, this requirement is necessary for patient safety and longer residency is only required for sentinel patients, to minimise inconvenience for participants. Participants will be compensated for their time and inconvenience.
* The contraception requirement may involve changes to lifestyle, however this requirement is necessary to minimise the risk of exposing a developing embryo or foetus to an untested drug.
* Questionnaires designed to assess the effects of the treatment on lifestyle may be considered a minor intrusion by participants.

Where is the study run from?
SASPiPhi Limited (UK).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
January 2027 to January 2029.

Who is funding the study?
SASPiPhi Limited (UK).

Who is the main contact?

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  Males and females aged 18 years to 60 years at the time of providing consent
2.  Participants must be willing and able to comply with trial requirements
3.  A diagnosis of CF by sweat chloride or presence of applicable CFTR gene variant
4.  Ability to produce sputum adequately for all study visits
5.  Pseudomonas aeruginosa from sputum or throat swab in the last 12 months
6.  As part of standard of care, CF patients are regularly tested for presence of infection related bacteria and assessment of this data will provide a pre screen so that only individuals with a reasonable likelihood of meeting the Pseudomonas aeruginosa inclusion criteria are taken forward to screening assessment
7.  Pseudomonas aeruginosa positive at the screening assessment with demonstrated susceptibility to SASPject PT3.9
8.  The ability to provide informed consent prior to any study specific procedures
9.  Women of childbearing potential and fertile male participants who are sexually active with women of childbearing potential must agree to use two methods of contraception and refrain from donating ova or sperm from first administration of trial treatment throughout the trial and up to 4 months after dosing
10. Post menopausal women defined as no menses for 12 months without an alternative medical cause and FSH greater than 30 IU/L
Exclusion criteria:
1.  Body weight less than 30 kg
2.  FEV1 less than 40 percent predicted
3.  Pregnant, breastfeeding or intending to become pregnant, where pregnancy is defined as the state of a female after conception until termination of gestation, confirmed by a positive urine human chorionic gonadotropin laboratory test
4.  Changes to standard CF therapy including channel modulators in the 3 months prior to dosing
5.  Active treatment of any mycobacterial or fungal organism within or equal to 30 days prior to dosing
6.  Any known allergy to any component of the investigational medicinal product, where SASPject PT3.9 is formulated in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM CaCl2, 5 mM MgSO4 and diluted 10 mL in 100 mL of 0.9 percent saline
7.  Acute clinical illness requiring a new oral, parenteral or inhaled antibiotic in the 30 days prior to dosing
8.  ALT or AST above the upper limit of normal, with retest allowed, or bilirubin above the upper limit of normal unless known Gilbert syndrome where the exclusion is greater than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, with retest allowed
9.  Clinically significant laboratory abnormalities not associated with the study indication at screening
10. Participants with hepatitis B or C, carriers of HBsAg, carriers of HCV antibodies or positive for HIV 1 or 2 antibodies
11. Primary immunodeficiency
12. Lung transplantation
13. Any active cancer or history of cancer with less than 5 years disease free survival time, except completely treated in situ carcinoma of the cervix or completely treated and resolved non metastatic squamous or basal cell carcinoma of the skin, with localized non metastatic basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma acceptable
14. Receiving medication likely to significantly suppress the immune system, including ciclosporin, tacrolimus, anti TNF alpha, corticosteroids greater than 15 mg per day, methotrexate, azathioprine, immunoglobulins or anti cytokines
15. Any significant medical condition recently diagnosed or not stable in the last 3 months, other than pulmonary exacerbations, that in the opinion of the investigator makes participation against the patient’s best interests
16. Participation in another interventional study within 3 months or 5 half lives, whichever is longer
17. Receipt of any vaccination including for Covid 19 within 28 days prior to first dose or planned vaccination within 3 months after the last dose of study medication
18. Use of any other investigational drug within 30 days prior to screening or 5 half lives, whichever is longer
19. Positive alcohol breath test or positive urine drug screen, with repeat assessment acceptable
20. Donation of blood in the 3 months prior to screening, plasma in the 7 days prior to screening or platelets in the 6 weeks prior to screening
